findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Functional
Case: normal use - a nightly waits for a runner while pull requests continue to merge.
The generated workflow checks out the scheduled event's commit, but `src/forge/fullrun.py:80` fetches current main and refuses before running tests if that commit is no longer the tip. The new gate then treats the workflow failure as a failed nightly, instructs the user to start a fix, and blocks story merges even though no test failed. Rerunning the scheduled workflow retains the original SHA, while a manually dispatched run cannot clear this gate. This can leave the team blocked until the next scheduled run. [GitHub documents the rerun SHA behavior](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/how-tos/manage-workflow-runs/re-run-workflows-and-jobs).
Adds work: handle a moved default branch in the scheduled full run; F 2 x H 2 = 4; 2 x C = 4
findings.title: Let queued nightlies run when main advances

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Not done
Case: normal use - a team prepares a release or sign-off after its last product merge.
The owner-approved item says: "No test run starts on main after a merge; the nightly full run is the only run on main, and Forge merges nothing while main's newest nightly result is red, naming the nightly run and the repair step; new and existing repos get it on upgrade and forge sync". The generated workflow still enables `workflow_dispatch` and its full-suite job runs for that event. The shipped guide at `src/forge/templates/skill.md:2302` tells teams to dispatch that full run on the default branch after the last product merge, so a non-nightly test run still starts there. The named workflow test checks that schedule is present and push is absent, but passes with this manual run enabled.

findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 1, Harm 3
Raise: Functional
Case: normal use - a repo uses human merges and a story task reaches `forge land` after the nightly fails.
The handoff still says the task is ready and that a human merges its pull request; the new note asks for a fix but removes the previous instruction to wait before merging the task. The `forge land --all` path at `src/forge/land.py:559` also classifies it under "Ready to merge". A human following that handoff can merge the task while the nightly is red. The new human-advice test asserts this same ready-to-merge message, so it does not catch the regression.
Adds work: retain the hold instruction in the human handoff; F 2 x H 2 = 4; 2 x C = 2
findings.title: Tell human mergers to hold the task while the nightly is red

findings.body:
Gain 2, Work 1, Harm 1
Case: normal use - `forge land --all` encounters a red nightly for an agent-merged story task.
The new refusal has no `Next:` line. The queue parser at `src/forge/land.py:589` looks for one, so its final summary either uses the earlier `Next: forge merge` from close or reports a generic exit code. It omits the failed run and repair step and directs the user to retry, even though the detailed refusal appeared earlier in the streamed output.
findings.title: Follow-up: Preserve nightly details in queue summaries

why: The run of related tests on main after each merge uses runners that waiting pull requests need, and it repeats the pull request's CI whenever main did not move between that CI and the merge
